name: manual_b98cb3
claim: A qualification freeze approval is proven human-in-the-loop evidence when the approving account completes a fresh interactive GitHub device-code login in its own browser (one-time code entered by the human; MFA where enabled) into a new isolated gh config directory, and the approve step then posts the digest-bound approval comment as that account. Verify it by reading the comment back through the API: it exists on the intended PR, is authored by an allowlisted account, and its body repeats the exact consumer, harness, manifest and coverage digests that the repo's freeze checker accepts. An agent may start the flow and verify the result but must not complete the login or post the approval itself; the one-time code is never recorded, and the marker is single-use, so a failed post means re-authenticate in a new directory. Bind approval to the exact harness commit and dispatch on that SHA, because any later push makes the approval stale.

decisions.notes: Used for the M1 qualification freeze approval (2026-10-16): the operator ran the scripted authenticate and approve flow locally, the approval comment was posted by an allowlisted account on the qualification PR, and the evidence-mode workflow accepted the record at the approved harness head. The pattern separates who may authenticate (the human) from who may verify and dispatch (the agent).
